I’m not going in a strict chronological order as it’d mean I’d have to explain the same things multiple times, but it does try to work chronologically overall along the video. Also sorry I’m not quoting everything you said when I respond to it so you’re probably gonna have to follow along the video if you want to know what part of your argument I’m referencing.

Firstly, I want to reinforce my argument about the killing game taking place in the real world, rather than a fictional world. You stated that Tsumugi implies that the characters and world are literally fictional, especially in Trial 6. What I mean by literally fictional is a complete work of fiction, meaning they are non-physical, fictional characters in a non-physical, fictional world, simply made up by Team Danganronpa. This was never implied. The reasoning for this in the doc was for some reason ignored, where I referred to a quote from Tsumugi saying:
To translate from Gundham’s wording, he essentially reiterates Hajime’s words, saying that “Your non-physical self is fabricated, unlike your physical body”.

So when Tsumugi says that they are fictional, she means that they’re fictional in the sense that everything that makes them themselves is gone and replaced with made up stuff, except their physical body. This essentially just makes them fictional characters, which is why she calls them as such. However, they’re still real in the sense that they have physical bodies.

If you believe that the characters originated from the outside world and came into the killing game, which is what the narrative states, then I’d like you to explain how they would’ve been converted from a real, physical person to a complete, non-physical work of fiction. If you say they took or replicated their consciousness or something to that effect, that doesn’t make sense considering everything that makes up their mind was changed in comparison to their past self in the outside world, so there would be no point in using a real person's consciousness just to override/change it.

If you believe, contrary to the narrative, that the characters were not literally taken from the outside world, and they were created within the killing game boundaries, then first I would like you to explain why you believe as such, considering you’re straying away from what the game has stated as fact. Secondly, I’d like you to explain the prologue, and why they needed to have their personalities and memories implanted. If they were completely fictional from the start, body and mind, they could’ve been written to have whatever personality and backstory was needed, so there’s no need to use convoluted technology to achieve that if their bodies weren’t real. This includes the idea of “copy pasting” by imitating someone who exists in the outside world by creating a fully fictional character that represents them.

I then stated that since they’re real, physical people, it means that the world they are in is real too, since real people cannot exist in a fictional world. Your response relied on your interpretation of the characters as fully fictional, but now that I’ve explained why they’re not, I hope it’ll make sense why it’s impossible for a physical person to exist in a fictional world, therefore both the setting and the characters must be real. To back this up, we have this quote from Tsumugi:

You stated that the reason Tsumugi did not prevent the actions of Kokichi and Shuichi despite allegedly having a script is because the script was imperfect, but you didn’t elaborate on this. How was this imperfect script created? What evidence is there to suggest the creation of this script happened? Why was it imperfect? You also stated she did prevent Shuichi’s actions, which isn’t true as he literally ended Danganronpa.

You stated that the fact that everyone is confused in the prologue and don’t know what’s going on before they receive the first flashback light means that either V3 is fictional or the other games were fictional/didn’t happen, otherwise they would have realised they were in a killing game since they should’ve seen the previous killing games and understood their situation. You acknowledged that Rantaro wasn’t confused because he survived the previous killing game, which means that one previous killing game is proven to occur. However, the other characters still don’t remember that, even though it did occur, likely published as season 52, so it’s safe to say their memories of past seasons of Danganronpa were erased with the Blackout Light.

You also stated that since everyone except Kokichi and Rantaro got to explore their labs, it means a script must’ve been used to predict when they would die and reveal their lab before that point. A small inaccuracy would be that Kaede didn’t get to explore her lab either. Regardless, the whole situation is really not so improbable that you need to jump to a script being the answer. At the start of Chapter 2, 6 people had open labs, while 8 people had closed labs. It’s easy to predict Keebo wouldn’t die, as he’s a robot created specifically to survive the killing game as his eyes are the audience's cameras and his inner voice was the audience survey. So the fact that no one with closed labs died was a 46% chance. In Chapter 3 it was a 64% chance. In Chapter 4 it was a 56% chance. And in Chapter 1 and 5, people with closed labs died. Of course, even with these fairly even percentages it would be lucky to have no one with closed labs die each time, but the fact that 3 people with closed labs died makes it much more probable. Also, I explain in my doc how Tsumugi often targets a specific person to be the culprit with the motives and with what is revealed in each area, making it more probable. Ultimately, there’s no reason to jump to the conclusion of there being a script because of this.

You said she wasn’t stated to have made characters, but there is evidence to the contrary. When Keebo’s personality was erased, she said “That makes me sad too, y’know? He was a character I created.” She also talks about coming up with Kaito’s character and giving him a virus too.

I will now explain why it’s illogical to assume Tsumugi was brainwashed into believing she is the mastermind. Firstly, it is canon that the flashback lights aren’t all powerful, and don’t work if you know they’re lies. In Trial 6, Tsumugi says:
“Even if we make more flashback light motives for you, you’d know they’re lies… So no matter how many flashback lights we provide, it’s more likely that nothing will happen.”

So we know that it would be impossible to use a flashback light to manipulate someone if they know the flashback lights are lies. However, Tsumugi is the one producing and distributing the flashback lights using the flashback light producer throughout the game, so she’d know that they’re fabricated, and her mind would reject the flashback light’s lies. Also, while it does seem strange at first that Tsumugi would be acting scared in the prologue when everyone’s memory would be wiped anyway, it makes sense logically. If she acted like her usual mastermind self, that would basically be telling everyone “hey, I’m the person who kidnapped you all”. Announcing to a group of 15 people that you’re their kidnapper is not the smartest move, even if the Monokubs were going to use the flashback lights on the group eventually, they need to be in the same place so they all get captured by the light, and she also can’t count on the Monokubs doing it in time before things escalate and the group turns on her, considering they messed up already. Keep in mind everyone needs to enter the game unscathed.

It’s true that it wasn’t Kokichi’s focus to find the mastermind, but it’s still impressive that she acted so well that he didn’t naturally discern any deceit when she was lying to everyone’s face (e.g. about not going to the basement in Trial 1).

Unethical just means morally wrong. So the outside world would view the morally wrong things that fictional characters say and do as comedic. I don’t think I worded that poorly. Also, the point of that feat is that she appealed to the people inside the killing game (by being normal) and the audience outside the killing game (by making references in otherwise tense situations).

No matter how advanced the technology, it’s illogical for a physical person to be able to exist in a non physical world, i.e. a simulation. If it was a simulation, that would make the people inside non-physical. Take DR2 for example, because they were inside the neo world, their bodies weren’t actually real inside of that world, instead, their bodies were sleeping in the real world.

The reason I said about her altering the flashback light manually is because when you’re playing as Shuichi it only shows multiple choice options on the screen, and there’s no option to make your own custom flashback light. However I admit that it is a highball to assume she altered the mechanisms of the flashback light, rather than assume there is just a feature to edit the flashback light via the machine.
